description: XGMML conformance corpus: Cytoscape's own reader test files (2.x and 3.x dialects, groups, lists, hidden and SUID columns), a 2.x session's network files, a Cytoscape 3.10 export, other producers (EFI-EST, NGSCheckMate, VPLG), and authored files for the XGMML 1.0 draft's examples, session network and view documents and every edge case of research-xgmml.md section 5. Expectations are hand-written from the specification until the Cytoscape oracle workflow runs (design 6.3); oracleDisagrees marks where Cytoscape departs from the specification.

fixtures.exercises: 2.x-style typed atts at all three levels, lists of string and integer, boolean 1, a self-loop, negative id -1, the label alias fills interaction
cy:type / cy:elementType; Integer versus Long under type=integer
graph-level lists: no type and no items (a list of strings, W_XGMML_EMPTY_LIST_TYPE), a typed empty list, a child without a value, a list holding an empty string
fixtures.oracleDisagrees: Cytoscape 3.10 creates no column for an untyped empty list (its element type is unknown); graph-io keeps it as an empty list of strings and says so, so the attribute is not dropped silently

fixtures.exercises: cy:hidden as 1 / 0 / true / false; an edge before its target node
*.SUID references (valid, dangling, string-typed) kept as typed values, never remapped
fixtures.oracleDisagrees: Cytoscape remaps *.SUID values to the SUIDs of the new session and drops unresolvable ones; SUIDs mean nothing outside the session that wrote them, so graph-io keeps the values as written with extra.suidReference

fixtures.exercises: bare & in attribute values, read with repairBareAmpersands (Cytoscape's 7-byte lookahead)
an empty graph
an empty graph with a DOCTYPE whose SYSTEM URL is dead (never fetched) and no namespace
no XGMML namespace or DOCTYPE (read with W_XGMML_NO_NAMESPACE), cy:documentVersion 3.0, 3.x graphics with nested visual properties, an empty __Annotations list
fixtures.oracleDisagrees: Cytoscape's file filter refuses a root graph without the namespace or an xgmml.dtd DOCTYPE; the content is unambiguous XGMML, so graph-io reads it and warns

fixtures.exercises: a collapsed 2.x metanode group: members only inside the node-nested graph, the nested graph's own att, a meta-edge
fixtures.oracleDisagrees: Cytoscape shows a collapsed group as its group node only (2 nodes, 1 edge in the visible network); graph-io's snapshot holds every node of the document and records the group as parent containment

fixtures.exercises: an expanded 2.x group: members referenced by xlink:href, the 2.x writer's repeated edges dropped
fixtures.oracleDisagrees: Cytoscape hides an expanded group's own node (3 nodes in the visible network); graph-io keeps the group node as the parent of its members

fixtures.exercises: groups inside groups (2.8.3): containment two levels deep
fixtures.oracleDisagrees: Cytoscape shows the collapsed outer group only (3 nodes, 3 edges); graph-io flattens every node and keeps the nesting as parent containment

fixtures.exercises: 2.x documentVersion 1.0 at full size: RDF metadata, a non-numeric root id, no directed attribute, att label= as the name, 1,324 lists, cytoscape*GraphicsAttributes, a single-quoted XML declaration, the ns1 XLink prefix
fixtures.oracleDisagrees: Cytoscape 3.10 never reads the root directed attribute and makes every edge without cy:directed directed (research-xgmml.md 4.2); the XGMML DTD says directed defaults to 0, so the expectation is undirected

fixtures.exercises: a Cytoscape 2.x session network file: graph view atts, cy:editable, nested_network_id pointers by network label
a Cytoscape 2.x session network file
a Cytoscape 2.x session network file
a Cytoscape 2.x session network file

fixtures.exercises: a node with a label but no id (the label is the id) and one with neither (E_MISSING_ID, skipped)

an edge id used twice: the second edge is skipped
fixtures.oracleDisagrees: Cytoscape 3 creates both edges; edge ids are unique in XGMML (the DTD's ID type) and in graph-io's id column

<graph/> alone
a whole network on one line (the tokenizer is not line-bound)
unknown elements under graph: skipped with their subtree, once per name
fixtures.oracleDisagrees: Cytoscape's state machine ignores the unknown tag but keeps descending, so it reads the node inside the wrapper; an element XGMML does not define has no meaning to read into, so graph-io skips the subtree and says so

fixtures.exercises: boolean spellings: yes, TRUE, 0 read; 2 is E_BAD_VALUE
fixtures.oracleDisagrees: Cytoscape reads any boolean text other than 1, true or yes as false, so 2 becomes false silently; graph-io does not guess and reports it

fixtures.exercises: cy:documentVersion="3.x": warned, the dialect is chosen from the content
a list whose items declare integer and string: widened to a list of strings
fixtures.oracleDisagrees: Cytoscape types the list by its first item and fails to convert x to an integer; design 5.1 widens to the type every item fits

a list att with a value, a scalar att with child atts and an att without a name: W_XGMML_BAD_ATT once per kind

Cytoscape 3 graphics: NETWORK_* graph graphics, nested visual-property atts, lockedVisualProperties, z as its own column (a WikiPathways-style 32768)

an xlink:href member naming no node, and an edge reference naming none
a nested-network pointer into another file, kept as text

a node in two 3.x groups (__isGroup): the parents list
root-level subgraphs of a generic document: flattened, membership in xgmml.networks

a Cytoscape 3 session network file (the structure of subnetworks.cys): three registered networks, shared nodes and edges by xlink:href, a cross-file pointer, a pointer to another subnetwork, a self-loop only in a subnetwork
a Cytoscape 3 session network file (the structure of nestedGroups_expanded.cys): group networks with cy:registered="0", multi-membership, meta-edges declared at the root only
fixtures.oracleDisagrees: Cytoscape reads G1 and G2 as groups from the session's hidden __isGroup table, which a network file alone does not carry; read on its own, the file's node-nested graphs are nested-network pointers (the .cys importer supplies the group bookkeeping)
